title: Starter sprint labs birdseye notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, experimental companion doc for a 3-session starter sprint intended to get a small engineering team from zero to a shipping prototype that calls Redwood’s SDK. The emphasis is: short microflows, pragmatic telemetry, one-hour lab templates, and resilient default fallbacks. This is intentionally lightweight — think: pocket notebook for a new hire pair or a customer workshop lead.

Audience:
- New hires in product/infra/SDK integrations (first 2 weeks)
- Solutions engineers running hands-on onramp workshops
- Internal SDK maintainers who need a reproducible one-hour lab to validate changes

Design constraints / guiding principles:
1) Sessions are 45–60 minutes long with clear, measurable outcomes.
2) Minimal prerequisites: laptop, Node/Python installed, Redwood demo token (or local stub).
3) Labs are written so a non-author can run them from the script.
4) Observe > change > ship: capture a tiny telemetry signal before and after tweaks.
5) Failure injection is deliberate: each lab includes a 5–8 minute chaos probe.

High-level plan (3 micro-sessions):
MAP (45m): orientation + quick API call + surface expectations
- Goal: first end-to-end call with SDK, see a streaming response, record latency and token counts.
- Steps: create token, run quickstart sample, capture trace id and token-count metric, validate output shape.
- Success criteria: sample app returns a coherent text response; telemetry entry with latency and token_count appears in the dashboard.

PROBE (60m): instrumentation + telemetry + edge-case tests
- Goal: add minimal instrumentation (request id, latency, retry count) and exercise 3 failure modes.
- Steps: add a wrapper that logs {req_id, start_ts, end_ts, token_count, status}; run 3 experiments: slow network (throttle), model fallback (force variant), and truncated payload (send malformed input).
- Chaos probe (5–8m): simulate 500 errors from the runtime and observe automatic fallback to smaller model variant. Confirm graceful degradation path.
- Success criteria: telemetry captures retries and fallback; user-visible latency increase documented but no crash.

SHIP (45–60m): sample feature + rollout checklist + smoke tests
- Goal: implement a minimal feature (autocomplete snippet or summarizer), add CI smoke test that runs against a stub, and create a rollout plan (canary + metrics to watch).
- Steps: write sample endpoint, add CI job to run quick smoke call with a hermetic stub, create feature flag gating in config.
- Success criteria: green CI smoke run; rollout doc updated, holdback percentage defined.

One-hour lab templates (scriptable):
- Before session: share quick repo link (see linked_artifacts). Ensure token or stub details are copied into .env.
- Minute 0–5: welcome, goal statement, safety/clobber note ("we will induce errors").
- Minute 5–25: guided walk-through of minimal sample app (run it).
- Minute 25–40: small modification (add logging/telemetry or change prompt).
- Minute 40–55: run chaos probe and capture results; discuss.
- Minute 55–60: wrap, next steps, assign a 2-day follow-up task.

Example microflow scripts (pseudocode):
- Node.js sample snippet to capture telemetry:
  const reqId = uuid(); const start = Date.now();
  try { const resp = await redwood.generate({prompt}); log({reqId, start, end: Date.now(), token_count: resp.tokens}); }
  catch (e) { log({reqId, error: e.message}); throw e; }

Failure modes & recovery checklist (practical):
- Network timeout: ensure client-level timeout < 3s for UI flows; on timeout, show cached suggestion and increment timeout metric.
- Transient 500s: implement exponential backoff with capped retries (max 3) and allow immediate fallback to a smaller model variant.
- Unexpected schema: validate server response shape, if mismatch increment schema-regression counter and route to a diagnostic bucket.

Minimal telemetry signal set (what to emit from labs):
- request_id (string)
- model_variant (string)
- latency_ms (numeric)
- token_count (numeric)
- status (ok | retry | fallback | error)
- fallback_reason (optional string)
Keep events tiny; emit once per request.

Observability quickwins for the lab:
- Create a short dashboard with 3 panels: 95th latency, token_count histogram, fallback rate. Use these panels for the canary during rollout.
- Add a trace link in logs to reproduce a failing request end-to-end.

CI smoke test pattern (lightweight):
- Use hermetic stub that deterministically returns predictable token_count and short latency.
- Single test assertion: returned.text startsWith("Hello") and telemetry.token_count == expected.
- Run smoke as a required gate for SDK PRs touching client-side code.

Rollout & gating knobs (suggested defaults):
- Canary: 3% traffic -> 15% -> full over 48h if metrics stable.
- Abort conditions: fallback_rate > 1% OR 95th_latency increases by >30% OR error_rate > 0.5% for 15m window.

Post-lab follow-ups (2-day action items):
- Create a short retrofit ticket to add an integration smoke test to the monorepo.
- Export the 3-panel dashboard to a named saved view and link in the feature PR.
- Run a retro: what broke during chaos probes and how to make the recovery path automatic.

Notes to the runner (ops tips):
- Keep the lab lightweight: if participants get blocked on credentials, switch to stub mode and continue.
- If someone modifies global configs, revert immediately and note the change for the retro.
- Encourage copying telemetry snippets into the PR body so reviewers can see empirical evidence.

Appendix: quick checklist for workshop lead
- [ ] Repo link shared and cloned
- [ ] Tokens/stub access validated
- [ ] Dashboard template loaded
- [ ] CI smoke stub job added
- [ ] Rollout thresholds drafted in PR

Open questions / things to iterate on:
- Should the default fallback model be a quantized variant or a smaller full-precision model? (tradeoffs: cost vs. quality)
- How granular should the telemetry be for token attribution per prompt segment?
- Is the hermetic stub approach sufficient to catch regressions in model output shape?

Recommended next doc steps:
- Convert this notebook into a 1-page facilitator script and a 2-page participant handout.
- Create a short video (6–8m) that runs the MAP session so new hires can prewatch.
- Wire a tiny sample CI job into the template repo referenced in linked_artifacts.

End of notebook.

Author notes: iterative draft; removed a lot of the older, long-form onboarding content to keep the sessions nimble. Please add feedback inline or create JIRA-ENGDX tickets for major changes.
